name: keycloak
summary: Identity and access management platform for SSO, OIDC, SAML, and tenant-aware authentication flows.
why_it_matters: Keycloak preserves important identity-platform capability knowledge, but no current project-level workflow justifies maintaining it as an active supported resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs centralized identity or SSO.
Operators want self-hosted OIDC or SAML infrastructure.
The workflow requires richer IAM capabilities than a lightweight auth helper.

platform_support.notes: Containerized deployment is portable, but real support requires clear guidance for realms, persistence, TLS, and identity-provider integration.

prerequisites: Container runtime and persistent database strategy
Defined TLS, backup, and operator workflows
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate one or two identity workflows instead of claiming broad IAM coverage.
Realm bootstrap and config export/import need explicit conventions.
Treat auth integration as higher risk than a generic compose stack.
operational_notes: Persistence and backup semantics are critical for identity systems.
Upgrade paths and realm migrations matter over time.
Validation should cover login and token issuance, not just startup.
risks: Identity infrastructure has high blast radius when support is shallow.
A broad wrapper would imply more operational maturity than currently exists.
